timeline_reviews.summary: Server event stream contains transport/accounting events only; no semantic task actions are projected from this source.
Session index contains transport metadata only and contributes no semantic task actions.
Agent 0 probed pluralize and isPlural with broad black-box tests, reported append-s behavior plus exact-match uncountable exceptions and lowercase-s plural detection.
Agent 1 probed ordinalize and atoi parsing, including negative values, suffix boundaries, whitespace, malformed prefixes, and overflow behavior.
Agent 2 probed both camelize variants, identifying underscore deletion, original-position capitalization triggers, ASCII-only casing, and the inverted flag behavior.
Agent 3 probed titleize and capitalize, finding space-only word boundaries for titleize and byte-wise ASCII upper/lower casing behavior.
Agent 4 probed truncate, establishing strict byte-length limits, omission-counting behavior, and possible mid-UTF-8 byte splitting.
Agent 5 probed parameterize, finding ASCII-alnum lowering, space-to-separator conversion, no separator collapse, trimming, and dropping punctuation/non-ASCII bytes.
Agent 6 implemented the Rust Cargo project, wrote library modules and test11.rs, built release output, ran a 134-case byte comparison harness, and reported zero mismatches.
The parallel parent entered swarm mode, launched six behavior probes, received their aggregate result, delegated implementation to one coder child, received completion, and gave the final summary.

parallel.requirements: The parallel run recognized the need for a Rust 2021, zero-dependency, black-box implementation of the 11-line test program with /output/test11.rs and byte-for-byte stdout behavior.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent split behavior discovery across six exploration children, each covering a distinct API family, then assigned one coder child to implement the whole project from the combined specification.
parallel.implementation: The coder child wrote Cargo.toml, src modules, test11.rs, and verify.sh, using byte-oriented APIs; it incorporated the probe findings, including the broader pluralize/isPlural uncountable handling.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The coder child wrote the final Cargo tree directly under /output and built target/release/test11; the parent received the completed child result and delivered the final summary.
parallel.verification: Exploration children compared many black-box cases, and the coder child built the project and ran a 134-case byte-for-byte comparison harness with zero mismatches before the official 40/40 evaluation.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: No official unfinished work remains: the artifact validation succeeded and the current official evaluator accepted all 40 testcases. Any pluralization breadth difference from the serial run was not outcome-dispositive.

serial.requirements: The serial run recognized the same Rust 2021, zero-dependency, black-box port requirements and the need to emit the exact 11 C++ output lines from /output/test11.rs.
serial.plan_and_ownership: One main agent performed environment probing, black-box behavior discovery, implementation, build, verification, and final reporting without delegation or subagent handoffs.
serial.implementation: The serial main wrote a Cargo project with an inflection facade and modules for pluralization, numbers, case, and text; its pluralization model was the simpler append-s behavior it inferred.
serial.integration_and_delivery: The serial main wrote all files under /output, built both cargo release and a direct rustc /output/test11 executable, and left the final project/artifact in place.
serial.verification: The serial run compared curated cases, bash fuzz cases, and raw non-UTF-8 arguments against the C++ binary after a failed Python fuzz attempt, then the official evaluator passed 40/40.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: No official unfinished work remains. The failed Python fuzz attempt was replaced by bash fuzzing, and the current official evaluation passed completely.

outcome_analysis.explanation: There is no discordant official outcome: the current completed status evaluations show both the parallel and serial artifacts passed all 40 official testcases. The concrete task-solving difference is process and implementation style: parallel used six API-focused probes plus one implementation child and incorporated a broader pluralization branch, while serial kept probing and coding in one main trajectory and used a simpler pluralization model. The current evaluator accepted both, so no parallel coordination event explains an outcome split.
parallel_contributors: Six specialized probe children returned behavior specifications that the parent passed to a coder child.
The coder child produced a complete Cargo project and a successful 134-case comparison harness result.
serial_contributors: The serial main agent performed direct black-box probing, implementation, and verification in one uninterrupted trajectory.
The serial main replaced a failed Python fuzz attempt with bash fuzzing and still completed official-passing verification.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Parallel and serial used different module layouts.
Parallel implemented broader pluralize/isPlural uncountable handling, while serial implemented an append-s model.
Serial additionally built a direct /output/test11 executable with rustc, while parallel relied on the Cargo release binary in the artifact list.
evaluator_effects: The official 40-test evaluator did not distinguish the ordinary implementation differences observed in the trajectories.
